@rekram1-node i’m hitting the same root cause from [herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr). herdr gives each pane its identity through client-local variables such as `HERDR_PANE_ID` and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`. with the shared service, a turn submitted from client b still runs with the environment of whichever client started the server.

i reproduced this on `opencode2 v0.0.0-next-17444`:

```text
server environment:  HERDR_PANE_ID=server-pane
client environment:  HERDR_PANE_ID=client-pane
shell tool received: HERDR_PANE_ID=server-pane
```

an opencode setting could list which client environment variables should be forwarded. the TUI would read those values and attach them to each turn, with tool calls and subagents inheriting that turn’s environment. storing static values in server config would not work because each attached client can belong to a different herdr pane.

`--standalone` works around this, but shared-server clients still cannot identify their originating pane.

Update for anyone finding this: the v2 `ctx.session.hook("http.request")` / `http.response` hooks now cover most of what was asked here — a plugin can mutate the outbound `Request` before dispatch. One gap remains: per the [v2 docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins) these hooks apply to **native models only; AI-SDK-routed models don't pass through them** (and `ctx.aisdk.hook` exposes the SDK/model, not the outbound request/body), so providers on a custom OpenAI-compatible `baseURL` still can't have their outbound requests intercepted — which blocks the secret-redaction/egress-audit use case from this issue for those providers. Opened a focused follow-up: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42846.

Checked the v1.18.18 source of `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-status.tsx`:

const path = fileURLToPath(value)
const parts = path.split("/")        // still splits on "/" only

A fix is proposed in #40132 (cross-platform split).

Thanks for the duplicate check — #36006 is indeed the same root problem and its proposals are excellent. I want to clarify one gap my report adds that #36006 does not cover: **images pasted from the clipboard have no local file path at all**.

### The paste scenario

When a user **pastes** an image (rather than `@`-referencing a file), the image never touches disk:
- It is stored as a `data:image/...;base64,...` URL inside the `part` table of `opencode.db` (verified: `{type:"file", mime:"image/png", filename:"image-2.png", url:"data:..."}` with `session_id`/`message_id`).
- `filename` is a synthetic name (`image-2.png`), not a path.

So for pasted images, **none** of #36006's options help directly:
- Option C (put the file path in the replacement text) — there is no path to put there.
- Options A/B (plugin hook / custom template pointing at a path) — same problem.

The only way to recover a pasted image is via the session/message/part identity (querying the local DB or the serve API `GET /session/:id/message`). The agent currently cannot know even the current `session_id` (no env var, no context injection).

### Concrete suggestion to cover both scenarios

If #36006's Option A hook were extended to include **the original part's identity** (or its `data:` URL) rather than only a file path, both scenarios would be covered:

```typescript
input: {
  sessionID: string
  messageID?: string
  partID?: string
  dataURL?: string       // for pasted media that never touched disk
  filename?: string
  mime: string
  ...
}
```

That way a plugin can guide the LLM to a tool that reads pasted images from the DB/serve API (which is exactly the workaround my team built: a skill that pulls the latest image part via the serve API and forwards it to a separate vision model).

Also worth noting: exposing the current `session_id` to agents (e.g. an `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` env var for tool calls) would fix the related issue #33035 and remove the need to guess the session at all.

Happy to consolidate this detail into #36006 if maintainers prefer a single issue.

## project rename silently fails for non-git projects (id "global")
 #42853

### Description

Renaming a project via the "Edit Project" dialog silently has no effect when the project's resolved ID is `"global"` (i.e., a plain/non-git folder, or a git repo with no remote, no commits, and no cached ID). The dialog closes but the displayed name never changes. Restarting, re-opening the project, or closing/re-adding the workspace does not help.

Root cause: for such projects the app's `save` path (`packages/app/src/components/edit-project.ts`) only performs the real update when `props.project.id` is set and not `"global"`:

```ts
if (props.project.id && props.project.id !== "global") {
  ... await sdk.client.project.update({ projectID: props.project.id, ... }) // real, persisted save
  return
}
serverCtx().sync.project.meta(props.project.worktree, { name, ... }) // dead store: never read
```

`Project.resolve` (`packages/core/src/project.ts`) returns `ID.global` for any directory that isn't a git repo, or whose repo has no remote / `.git/opencode` cache / root commit:

```ts
if (!repo) return { id: ID.global, ... }
return { id: id ?? ID.global, ... }
```

The fallback `sync.project.meta(...)` writes to `childStore.projectMeta` (localStorage), but that store is write-only in the codebase — `enrich()` (`global.tsx` / `layout.tsx`) only ever reads the server's `data.project`. So the rename appears to succeed (dialog closes) but is never persisted or displayed.

**Plugins**

None (OpenCode Desktop, default plugins).

**OpenCode version**

1.18.18 (OpenCode Desktop;)

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a brand-new empty folder (no git), or run `git init` in a folder but do **not** commit / add a remote.
2. In OpenCode Desktop (old layout) click **+** to add that folder, then open it.
3. Open the project's **Edit Project** dialog and change the default name to something new, then click **Save**.
4. The dialog closes, but the name in the sidebar stays unchanged.
5. Repeat after restarting the app, after re-opening the project, and after closing + re-adding the workspace — the rename still has no effect.
6. (Control) Repeating the same steps on a folder that is a git repo **with at least one commit or a remote** works fine.

**Operating System**

Windows 11

**Terminal**

N/A — OpenCode Desktop (Electron app), old layout

I started digging into this to find where `events.persist` is wired so I could thread it through `opencode2 serve`, but I can't locate the flag and want to share what I found before proposing a fix.

**What I checked (on `dev` @ 4643e65):**

- `packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/types.gen.ts` — `ServerConfig` has `port | hostname | mdns | mdnsDomain | cors` only. No `events` field, no `persist`.
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts` — 24 lines; calls `Server.listen(opts)` with network options only, no persist flag.
- `packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts` — `ListenOptions` has `port | hostname | mdns | mdnsDomain`, no `persist`.
- `packages/core/src/event.ts` — `EventV2.publish` → `commitDurableEvent` → `db.insert(EventTable)` inside a transaction (~line 337). I don't see a `persist: false` code path; durable rows appear to be written on every publish when a DB is configured.
- `packages/opencode/src/event-v2-bridge.ts` and `.../httpapi/server.ts` — `EventV2.node` is wired in unconditionally; no persist toggle at the layer boundary.

GitHub code search for `events.persist` across the repo returns 0 hits, and no commit in history mentions it.

**To make sure I'm looking at the right thing:**

1. Is `events.persist` defined in a config schema or branch I'm not seeing — a private fork, a docs-only spec, or a field that was renamed?
2. The repro says "durable event payload rows were not retained." Given that `commitDurableEvent` inserts on every publish, could the symptom have a different cause — DB path not pointing where expected, migration `20260323234822_events.ts` not applied to the target DB, or events going through a non-`publish` path?
3. If `events.persist` is intended-but-not-yet-implemented, I'm happy to help add it — just want to confirm the intended shape (env var? yargs flag? `ServerConfig` field?) before drafting, so I don't add a flag that duplicates an existing path under a different name.

Not trying to dismiss the report — `opencode2 serve` is a real entry point (`packages/desktop/scripts/utils.ts`) and the symptom you describe is worth fixing. I just want to pin down the config shape before proposing code.
Also seeing this issue with Qwen3.8-27b. Disabling Context 7 MCP on the session stops the issue occuring.

#42771 is ready for review and now carries both halves:

- **Eviction** (rate): `summary.diffs` patch text moves to a `message_diff` side table; `message.updated.1` drops from ~432 KB avg / 63 MB peak to ~4 KB avg for diff-carrying events. Running in production since 2026-08-15 on the 51 GB database this issue was measured on — numbers and compatibility notes are in the PR body.
- **Retention** (stock): opt-in `retention.event_idle_days` — hourly sweep deleting event history (events + sequence allocator, so revival restarts at seq 0 without a gap) for sessions idle beyond the threshold. Projected state untouched; swept sessions still render fully.

One operational data point beyond the PR body: with both landed plus a one-time cleanup of pre-existing event stock, the database here went 51.3 GB → 5.5 GB, and the recurring `database is locked` warnings from a second process reading the same file stopped. Setup: 23 plugins declared in `opencode.jsonc`, plus (separately) every file auto-loaded from `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` whether or not it's in the config array — that second set alone added another ~19 files/68 tools I hadn't accounted for.

| | tools | schema tokens (chars/4 estimate) |

Then cross-referenced against `magic-context`'s `tool_definition_measurements` table (real tokenizer counts, not chars/4 — the estimate above was off by up to 7.8x on individual tools) and against actual invocation history in `opencode.db`: **178 of 214 registered tools had zero invocations across 404 sessions**, while still costing schema tokens on every single request.

Scoping the dead ones out via per-agent `permission: {tool_or_glob: "deny"}` (confirmed it strips the schema, doesn't just block execution — verified with `opencode debug agent <name>`) took one orchestrator agent from 126,643 → 78,983 measured input tokens on an identical prompt, a 37.6% cut, without losing any capability (denies don't cascade to subagents, so everything stays reachable by delegation).

Hi @thdxr @nexxeln — FYI we have a working implementation on the `task-resume` branch of https://github.com/linsmod/opencode: - `/resume {msg}` — deterministically re-prompts the interrupted subagents of the current turn; the parent stays busy while they run and their results flow back into the task parts (no synthetic message). - `resume_subagents` + `read_subagent_history` tools — the main agent can autonomously resume its own interrupted subagents (no session ids needed) and inspect their history; results are written back into the original task parts so the TUI updates in place. - Interrupted `task` parts carry a `resumable` marker (session id) in the model context; cancellation cascades to running children, and resume reuses the existing subagent session instead of spawning fresh ones. After ESC (cancel) or CTRL+C (abort), you can send a message asking to resume, or use `/resume` to resume the uncompleted subagent tasks of that turn, and the main task will wait for all of them and go on as expected. We deliberately skipped graceful pause — cancel + resume covers it.
